analyst_view.overall: Elche (17th, 10 points) are still looking for their first home league win of the season, while Betis arrive 4th on 23 points after a 2-1 Champions League defeat at Borussia Dortmund in midweek, one report says. Elche are without Marc Aguado and Thomas Lemar; Betis are without the suspended Facundo Bernal and the injured Cucho Hernández, but Junior Firpo and Álvaro Fidalgo are expected back.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Elche coach Martín Anselmi said he expects a 'more open' game than recent ones against Celta and Valencia, because Betis do not sit deep and are dangerous on the counter. Betis have conceded 10 in their last six and are coming off a midweek trip to Dortmund, so there should be spaces at both ends.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Anselmi wants Elche to control the ball and stay patient, and Betis like to break quickly rather than lay siege. Nothing in the news pushes the corner count clearly up or down.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards. Elche are 17th and under some pressure at home, but Anselmi has played down any anxiety about their missing home win. No referee was listed when we checked, so we stay with the model.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, which already assumes a busy game. Anselmi's expectation of an open match supports a high total. With Fer Niño and Troy Parrott leading the lines and Isco and Ezzalzouli expected for Betis, we see no reason to go above the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. An open, transition-heavy game against a Betis side that has leaked goals lately should produce clear chances. Fer Niño already has six league goals for Elche, which also points to more efforts on target.
